simd_decision.result: no std::arch/AVX2 route; normalisation made branch-free and table-driven instead (safe code, bit-identical)
simd_decision.measured_probe: throwaway single-file probe outside the repo, 24 MP RGGB, one thread: scalar normalise 40-60 ms, SSE2 intrinsics 15-29 ms, branch-free portable loop 16.7 ms; both fast variants bit-identical to scalar on all 24 M sites (IEEE binary64 division and binary32 conversion are correctly rounded per lane)
simd_decision.why_no_intrinsics: (1) the compiler requires unsafe to call a #[target_feature] function from a non-annotated caller even on x86_64 where sse2 is baseline, which conflicts with the crate #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; (2) the portable loop is as fast as the SSE2 version in the probe; (3) ExecutionHint::Sse2 -> unsupported_execution and route "scalar" are pinned by tests/develop_recipe.rs and stay; (4) estimated (single-thread probe divided by 16, not measured in situ) the normalise stage is about 1 ms of roughly 200 ms at 16 threads, so AVX2 runtime dispatch would not change the result
